# Select by color

- Route: `/tools/select-by-color`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `photo`
- Slug: `select-by-color`

## Summary

Pick a color with the eyedropper, widen the range with fuzziness, and adjust only that selection. (Photo editing)

## Details

Color range is one of the six mask kinds in the Aperture Masks panel, and it is the way to select by color: give any adjustment layer a mask, add a Color range component, click a color in the photo with the eyedropper, and every pixel whose color is close to it is selected. Closeness is measured as the CIE Lab distance between the pixel and the sampled color, and Fuzziness sets how far that distance may reach. Shift-click adds more sample colors, up to 8, and the selection takes the strongest match. Feather softens the edge, Invert flips it, Mask strength scales it, and the Mask view shows it as a red overlay or on its own. The mask is computed from the source photo and previewed instantly; the export renders the same mask on the original.
### What it does
- Samples a color from the photo with an eyedropper and selects pixels by their Lab color distance to it, which tracks how different the colors look rather than how different the RGB numbers are.
- Adds up to 8 target colors with shift-click and takes the maximum weight over all of them, so a sky with two blues or a jacket with highlights and shadows selects as one.
- Scales the selection radius with Fuzziness from 0 to 100, a Lab distance of 0 to 60, with a smooth roll-off over the outer half of the radius.
- Combines with other mask components by Add, Subtract or Intersect, then applies Mask feather, Invert and Mask strength to the folded result.
- Drives any adjustment: a Local adjustment for exposure, tone and saturation, an HSL layer for hue shifts, Levels, Curves or a black and white conversion limited to the selection.
### How to use it
1. Drop the photo and pick an adjustment: The Masks panel opens. Add a Local adjustment or select an existing layer and add a mask to it.
2. Add a Color range and click: Choose Color range, press Pick a color and click the color you want. Shift-click to add up to 8 colors.
3. Tune fuzziness and view the mask: Turn Mask view to Overlay and raise Fuzziness until the whole region is red; add a Subtract component if it spills.
4. Adjust and export: Set the layer sliders; only the selection changes. Export JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or TIFF, rendered from the original.
### Supported formats
- Input: JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF, HEIC, HEIF, AVIF, TIFF, BMP
- Output: JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, TIFF
- The mask is parametric (sampled colors, fuzziness, feather) and is re-rendered on the original at export, so it costs nothing in project size.
- Heavily compressed JPGs have blocky chroma that can give a ragged selection edge; a little Mask feather hides it.
### Technical details
- Each target color and each source pixel are converted from sRGB to CIE Lab (D65, standard matrix, with the 216/24389 linear segment). The distance is Delta E 76, the Euclidean distance over L, a and b. With Fuzziness f the radius is R = f/100 times 60 Lab units, and the weight is 1 - smoothstep(0.5 R, R, Delta E): full selection within half the radius, a cubic fade to zero at the radius. Over several targets the pixel takes the maximum weight; with no target the component is 0.
- A sky sampled at sRGB (92, 150, 214), Lab (60.7, -0.2, -38.4), at Fuzziness 20 (R = 12) selects a lighter patch of the same sky at (110, 165, 222), Delta E 7.1, with weight 0.91, and rejects a deeper blue at (60, 120, 200), Delta E 15.6, entirely. At Fuzziness 40 (R = 24) the deeper blue is included with weight 0.78 while a cloud at (235, 238, 240), Delta E 49.8, and a leaf green, Delta E 83.8, remain at 0 even at Fuzziness 60.
- Components fold left to right: Add is max(m, value), Subtract is min(m, 1 - value), Intersect is min(m, value). The folded mask is then blurred with a Gaussian whose sigma is feather/100 times 0.05 times the long side, 30 px at Mask feather 10 on a 6000 px photo, then inverted if Invert is on and multiplied by Mask strength, clamped to 0..1. The layer output is lerp(input, adjusted, mask).
- The color range reads the geometry-corrected source photo, not the output of earlier layers, so a selection does not change when you edit layers below it, and the same sampled colors select the same pixels in the preview and in the server render.
- The Aperture preview is drawn on your GPU (WebGL2) from a 1920 px copy, the exported file is rendered on our server from the original at full resolution with the same formulas, and the two agree within a small documented tolerance: color operations such as the adjustment under this mask are held to a mean error of at most one 8-bit level, a 99th percentile of 2 and a maximum of 4, and grain is bit-exact.
### When not to use it
A color range selection is the wrong tool when the subject shares its colors with the background, such as a person in a green shirt on grass; use Select subject, the AI mask, or a brush instead. It also struggles on gray scale or very desaturated photos, where every pixel sits within a few Lab units of every other and fuzziness cannot separate them; a Luminosity range mask does better there. If you want to shift one hue everywhere in the photo, the HSL ranges on the Change image color page already do that without any mask.
### Use cases
- Deepen a sky without touching the clouds: Sample the blue, Fuzziness 35, then a Local adjustment with Exposure -0.4 and Saturation +15; the clouds at Delta E near 50 stay out.
- Change the color of a product: Sample the shirt, shift-click its shadow and highlight, then an HSL layer with Hue shifted; the background is untouched.
- Even out skin tone: Sample a mid-skin value with Fuzziness 25, Mask feather 6, then lower Saturation slightly and lift Shadows on the selection.
- Gray everything except one color: Select the color, Invert the mask, and add a Black and white layer with that mask so only the selected color stays.
### FAQ
Q: How is fuzziness measured?
A: As a CIE Lab Delta E 76 distance. Fuzziness 100 is a radius of 60 Lab units; a pixel inside half the radius is fully selected and the selection fades to nothing at the full radius with a smoothstep.
Q: How many colors can I sample for one selection?
A: Up to 8 per Color range component, added with shift-click. Each pixel takes the strongest match among them, and you can add a second component if you need more.
Q: Can I remove part of the selection?
A: Yes. Add another component in Subtract mode, for example a brush over the spill or a second color range sampled on the unwanted color, and it is removed with min(m, 1 - value).
Q: Why does the selection include shadows of a different brightness?
A: Lab distance counts lightness as well as hue, so a shadow of the same hue 20 L units darker is about Delta E 20 away. Lower the fuzziness, or intersect with a Luminosity range to restrict the brightness.
Q: Can I see the mask on its own?
A: Set Mask view to Mask only for a gray scale view, or to Overlay to see it as red over the photo. The M key cycles the views while a mask is selected.
Q: Does the selection change when I edit other layers?
A: No. Color range reads the source photo after geometry, never the output of layers below, so adjusting exposure underneath does not shift the mask.
